To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

children are interested in using new technology for picture-taking; they are motivated to do this because of their interest in the technology and because of their desire to share the pictures with others; they are not interested in manipulating the pictures in ways that are considered to be photofakery; they have a sense of what is appropriate and inappropriate in the context of picture-taking; and their sense of what is and is not appropriate is similar to that of adults.
children take pictures to document, to create a record of their lives, and to share those pictures with others.
children use digital cameras and other technology for picture-taking in ways that are similar to and different from adults.
In summary, our research is concerned with
how children's pictures are taken, and the implications of children taking pictures.
children's use of digital photography and the implications for the development of their visual literacy.
the ways children are using new technology to make pictures and how they use those pictures.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
children take pictures for a variety of purposes, including documenting their lives and sharing them with others.
children use technology to take pictures in a variety of ways, for a variety of purposes, in a variety of contexts.
children take pictures for a variety of reasons and in a variety of situations and that the pictures they take can be manipulated and changed in a variety of ways.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
children use new technology in a similar fashion to adults and that children use new camera and Web technology in similar ways to how they use old technology.
children are not just consumers of pictures, they are also picture-takers, and they are doing things with pictures that adults are only beginning to do.
children are using new technology in creative and innovative ways.
The main takeaway from our work is that
children use new technologies for picture-taking in ways that we might not expect.
children are very much like us when it comes to picture-taking.
we need to think about children as active picture-takers, rather than just passive subjects.
